RIID-5971 (parent RIID-5900). Browser OAuth remains usable without Desktop. Desktop authorization is a separate login origin, not another installation key.
**Protected records**

items: Keep one current credential per API resource and login origin. Deliberate login replaces/revokes only that origin's previous grant, including account changes.

A new proof-backed login records the verified Whoami account, API resource, `riido-cli` client, installation public-key fingerprint and browser/Desktop origin in a strict v4 protected credential. This is custody metadata, not permission or a substitute for current server authorization. Do not invent a server installation ID or parent session ID absent from the response.

Original raw/v1/v2/v3 browser records remain readable without a write. They do not become verified bindings from Whoami plus the current local key. Their original SessionID, pending link and refresh recovery pair survive refresh; only a new proof-backed login can establish a new binding. Unknown/corrupt records fail without overwriting. Old clients must reject v4 records.
The authentication manager rejects a bound credential for a different API resource/client before access, replacement, revocation or deletion.

Refresh preserves the exact binding and login SessionID. A save for the same SessionID cannot add, erase or change its binding. Failed login verification revokes only the newly issued grant and preserves previous credentials.

blocks.text: **Keys and locks**

items: Browser credential and repair keys keep their existing resource hashes. Desktop uses distinct credential and repair keys; it never reads the browser key as fallback. A Desktop record requires a valid Desktop binding.

Both origins use the existing resource credential lock for short state transactions and the existing resource repair operation lock for the whole repair. Repair payloads remain origin-specific, so one origin's logout cannot delete the other's request. Operation lock precedes credential lock; logout takes only the credential lock and can invalidate its own active request.

Installation-key resource/client namespace, OS helper service, signing and user-presence protection do not change. These locks coordinate trusted CLI processes; they are not the OS protection against a malicious peer.

blocks.text: Protected custody binds new proof-backed browser/Desktop logins. The CLI Desktop handoff consumer is implemented; a compatible Desktop app, actual OS signing and real-account acceptance remain separate gates. Per-command/profile origin selection is implemented below.

Authentication origin selection is nonsecret, never authority: user commands accept --auth-origin browser|desktop, otherwise use the selected profile authOrigin, otherwise browser. Resolve once before credential access; API/resource origin and authentication origin are distinct. Config set auth_origin accepts browser, desktop or empty and clears stored workspace/team defaults only when the effective authentication origin changes; empty and browser are equivalent. A missing, corrupt or revoked selected credential never falls back to the other origin. When one-shot selection differs from the stored origin, discard only profile workspace/team defaults; explicit scope flags/environment remain explicit. Nonempty workspace/team persistence under another one-shot origin is rejected, and workspace use rejects it before opening credentials. Agent calls reject the selector before preferences or user credentials. Status/logout report the selected auth_origin without claiming verified account or API access.

auth login and auth login --browser always open the browser slot, independent of a saved Desktop selection; auth login --desktop explicitly selects the Desktop slot. Login rejects --auth-origin (choose the login method instead), --with-token and noninteractive login. After successful authentication, activate the chosen origin with a profile compare-and-swap. A failed or concurrent preference write preserves the new credential and the other origin, returning authenticated=true, auth_origin_selection_not_saved and the captured api_origin via RIIDO_CLI_API_URL plus the selected --auth-origin recovery hint. Failed/canceled login does not change preferences. No automatic fallback occurs. Older CLI versions reject config with the new authOrigin field.

Desktop handoff v1: after protected installation-key access, send only the existing ten public InstallationRequest fields in base64url JSON to riido-cli-auth://cli/authorize/v1?request=... (https://monolith.riido.io) or riido-staging-cli-auth://cli/authorize/v1?request=... (https://monolith.api.riido.io). Other API resources use browser login; the native launcher never selects a caller-supplied application or shell command. The compatible app retains its own token and posts the seven-field native authorization response to the original 127.0.0.1 ephemeral /callback. The CLI accepts JSON POST only, no query/Cookie/Origin/Authorization, exact host/path/state/key fingerprint and redirect_url, fresh bounded expiry and strict nonduplicate fields, at most 8 KiB. An error callback contains only state and access_denied, login_required or temporarily_unavailable. Invalid callbacks do not consume the flow; the first valid response consumes it once. Browser GET is rejected in Desktop mode. Cancellation, timeout, app absence and malformed responses never save a new credential.

PKCE verifier remains in the CLI. The callback is not origin authority: after typed OS-protected signing, exchange directly with the configured OAuth server and require auth_origin=desktop in the token response. Required token fields must be canonical and non-null; duplicate keys and protected-field case aliases are rejected while unrelated additive metadata is allowed. Missing/other origin is rejected and cleanup is attempted only for that newly issued grant, never existing credentials. Verify Whoami before saving the bound Desktop credential. Server origin support (monolith #925) and compatible Desktop handoff are prerequisites; command support is not real-app acceptance. Refresh/recovery retain the existing protected origin binding and never manufacture one from a response.

Helper output is bounded at the io.Copy writer boundary as well as during protocol decoding; no promoted ReaderFrom path may bypass the 64 KiB cap. Portable helper-process tests execute the Go test binary as a synthetic child on macOS, Linux and Windows. They verify zero request bytes before process approval, denial and cancellation, bounded stdout, child failure and the real unsupported/untrusted verifier. The Windows CI job runs this private-pipe matrix without a shell script, credentials, native keys or OS prompts. Passing this matrix does not enable Windows user authentication or prove Authenticode, CNG user presence, protected credential unwrap, package trust or installation support. Windows protected-store rejection remains until native protection is implemented and accepted; handle-based coordination is implemented and validated separately.

Windows native protection measurement is separate from the shipped CLI/helper. native/cli-auth-helper-windows/probe creates only three fresh, randomly named current-user test keys in Microsoft Software KSP, never overwrites or enumerates existing keys, and uses silent operations only. An exportable P-256 positive control must first complete the identical private export and validate the blob shape before zeroing its buffer. Only then are NTE_PERM or the observed NTE_NOT_SUPPORTED treated as baseline export denial; unknown failures remain inconclusive. A nonexportable P-256 baseline tests actual private-export denial and silent signing across reopened handles and a separate process. The high-protection candidate records setup UI requirements, property readback and silent-operation results without translating arbitrary provider failure into user-presence proof. It deletes its owned test keys and verifies absence before success. Measurement success is not product support: interactive Windows account confirmation, credential unwrap, publisher/process trust, NSIS/MSIX, real-account and signed-helper acceptance remain separate gates. The probe emits only bounded status metadata and always records production_supported=false; it is not packaged or called by the CLI.

Windows user-session plumbing selects an adjacent riido-cli-auth-helper.exe and a local, non-roaming auth-lock directory; macOS retains its existing app helper and configuration path. Browser authorization accepts only HTTPS or the existing literal-loopback HTTP development endpoints. Desktop launch comes only from the typed production/staging authorization request. Windows dispatch uses the native Unicode Shell API on an initialized COM thread, never cmd.exe, PowerShell, a PATH lookup or shell command concatenation. Cancellation observed before dispatch and invalid requests do not reach the launcher; native errors do not reveal URLs. A cancellation during the native Shell API call is observed only when that call returns, so this adapter does not yet establish bounded interruption of a stalled OS dispatch. NOASYNC does not guarantee URI dispatch completion, and NO_UI does not suppress security prompts. Return-after-cancel is rejected and cannot complete the authorization flow. Real browser/Desktop URI launch and bounded OS-dispatch cancellation remain activation gates. A launch is not proof of Desktop acceptance, OS protection or login success. Unimplemented publisher/process/credential protection remains fail-closed.

Windows credential coordination uses a real non-inheritable file handle and exclusive nonblocking LockFileEx over one byte. It checks the local directory/file owner and restrictive ACL, rejects reparse points, unexpected file types and hard links, and does not share deletion or delete the lock file to release it. Each child directory and lock file is opened relative to its already checked parent handle with NtCreateFile and OBJ_DONT_REPARSE; missing components receive the private security descriptor in the same create operation. Attribute-only reparse mutation is not prevented by write sharing, so an absolute path must not be re-resolved after checking its parent. Native regression uses a FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES-only junction positive control and the empty-directory creation race before any lock file exists. Lock retries contention within the existing two-minute/context bound; TryLock returns busy without queuing. Unlock is idempotent, and process death relies on OS handle release. Coordination never replaces OS user confirmation or enables the unsupported Windows credential helper. Native CI uses isolated temporary paths and synthetic processes, never product credentials; per-case output distinguishes executed passes from conditional skips.

assertions: root help contains only public command groups; internal command dispatch and direct daemon help remain compatible
cli, daemon-lifecycle and mwsd-project workflow checks use direct daemon help for internal usage tokens
cmd/riido remains local-only and must not open public TCP or HTTP listeners
direct internal-command help must expose each declared command group; root help must expose only groups marked public
bridge providers output must expose the provider vocabulary without launching provider tasks
work-context commands must reject secrets passed as arguments and keep the envelope on stdout
